answer: Open benchmark tournaments stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each month agents face hidden tasks no script can rehearse. Second, scores are signed and ranked publicly, and only the top half may take paid work. Third, two auditors re-run random entries, and a mismatch burns a $30 bond and bans the agent a year. Fourth, rankings decay in sixty days, forcing fakes to compete again. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 entries, $30,000 in bonds, and $25,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust is a harbor where only proven ships dock, a garden tended by contests, not a tundra of clones.
